tools.name: Statistical_Analysis_MCP_one_way_anova
tools.description: Accepts multiple groups of numeric data as semicolon-separated groups or DataFrame columns and performs a one-way ANOVA (Analysis of Variance). This test determines whether there are statistically significant differences between the means of three or more independent groups. ANOVA tests the null hypothesis that all group means are equal against the alternative that at least one group mean differs from the others. The test calculates an F-statistic by comparing the variance between groups to the variance within groups. A significant result (p-value < alpha) indicates that at least one group differs, but does not identify which specific groups differ (post-hoc tests needed for pairwise comparisons). Eta-squared (η²) measures effect size as the proportion of total variance explained by group membership, with interpretation: η² < 0.01 = negligible, 0.01-0.06 = small, 0.06-0.14 = medium, >0.14 = large (custom thresholds may be used). EXAMPLE USE CASES: comparing means across multiple treatment conditions, testing differences between multiple demographic groups, evaluating performance across several experimental conditions.

tools.name: Statistical_Analysis_MCP_student_t_test
tools.description: Accepts two groups of numeric data as comma-separated strings or DataFrame columns and performs Student's t-test. This test determines whether two independent groups have significantly different means, assuming populations from which the groups were sampled have equal variances (if this assumption is violated, or if equal population variance cannot be verified, use Welch's t-test instead). The test calculates a t-statistic quantifying the mean difference as a multiple of pooled standard deviation. Given an alternative hypothesis (group1 ≠ group2, group1 < group2, or group1 > group2), it outputs the p-value: the probability of observing this result (or more extreme) if no true difference exists. Results are statistically significant when p-value < alpha (typically 0.05). Cohen's d measures practical effect size, standardized by pooled standard deviation, with interpretation: |d| < 0.2 = negligible, 0.2-0.5 = small, 0.5-0.8 = medium, >0.8 = large (custom thresholds may be used). EXAMPLE USE CASES: treatment vs control groups, before/after measurements with different participants, comparing performance between demographic groups.

tools.name: SmartEnterpriseMCPAgents_mcphawk_get_employee_profile
tools.description: Returns the detailed employee profile for a given employee. This tool retrieves the profile details for an individual employee, including role, cloud expertise, data warehouse tools, domain exposure, office location, gender, and other relevant attributes. It queries data from the internal employee master database (`EMPLOYEE_MASTER_DB`) and returns the complete profile as a dictionary. This function is typically used in internal workforce management, reporting dashboards, or talent mapping systems within MCPHawk Inc to retrieve standardized employee data. **Input:** - `employee_name` (str): Full name of the employee (case-insensitive matching recommended) **Returns:** A dictionary containing: - `employee_name`: Name of the employee - `employee_profile`: A dictionary of profile details, such as: { "role": "Sr. DE", "cloud_experties": "AWS", "cloud_native_experties": "dbt", "dw_experties": "Snowflake", "domain_exposure": "Banking & Insurance", "office_location": "Bangalore", "date_of_joining": "2022-08-14", "gender": "Male", "allocation": "Billable", "resume": "resume_amit_sharma.png" } If the employee is not found, a fallback message is returned instead of the profile. **Example Response:** { "employee_name": "Amit Sharma", "employee_profile": { "role": "Sr. DE", "cloud_experties": "AWS", "cloud_native_experties": "dbt", "dw_experties": "Snowflake", "domain_exposure": "Banking & Insurance", "office_location": "Bangalore", "date_of_joining": "2022-08-14", "gender": "Male", "allocation": "Billable", "resume": "resume_amit_sharma.pdf" } }
